text:
taylor: Heads up — us-west2 racks showing sustained GPU saturation and noisy-MIG interference this morning. seeing frequent preemptions on fractional tenants and elevated pcie stall rates. thinking about a MIG-balanced carveout + small dedicated carveout for top noisy tenants + routing-weight shifts as a short-term mitigation. thoughts?

anya: can you drop the dashboard link? need the percentiles before we scope changes. also which tenants are top noisy? @chris did you get the tenant heatmap?

chris: link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/fg123/gpu-heatmap?orgId=1&from=now-3h to=now — us-west2-rack12 and rack14 are the hot ones. top noisy tenants are t-analytics, t-search, t-embed. warm-pool is ~60% filled rn.

devops-bot: ALERT: us-west2 rack12 GPU util > 92% (3m avg) — kernel_pcie_stalls spike 1.8x — incident id INC-7001

mike: MIG isolation helps but we've seen cross-vGPU bandwidth contention on these cards (nvlink less relevant, pcie root complex is the choke). if we carve small dedicated slices we need to ensure they land on separate root complexes to be effective.

lina: scheduler note — we can implement a temporary allocation rule: prefer non-saturated racks for heavy allocations, and apply a per-tenant cap on fractional slices. fallback routing to us-west1 will add ~8–12ms p50 for some regions. is that acceptable for search?

anya: curious about costs. if we bump warm-pool prefill + create 3 dedicated 1-card carveouts, what's rough monthly delta? chris?

chris: rough back-of-envelope: 3 dedicated cards reserved = ~ $8k/mo in amortized infra + warm pool increased by 20% (approx 5 GPUs warm) ~ $6k/mo. so ~ $14k/mo. routing churn and cross-AZ egress maybe +$500–1k depending on traffic shift.

anya: proposed playbook (short):
1) create 3x 1-card dedicated carveouts for top noisy tenants (temp 2 weeks)
2) apply MIG rebalance across cards in rack12/14 to spread vGPU slots (MIG profiles: 7g.40gb -> mix 3x7g/1x20g)
3) increase warm-pool prefill by +20% in us-west2 for 3h canary window
4) apply scheduler weight change: reduce fractional allocation weight to 0.6 for noisy tenants
5) monitor (p50/p95 latency, pcie_stalls, kvcache warm rate)

commands (canary):
```
# create carveout for tenant t-analytics
fleetctl carveout create --region=us-west2 --racks=rack12,rack14 --cards=1 --tenant=t-analytics --ttl=14d
# rebalance MIG across target hosts
fleetctl mig rebalance --hosts rack12-host[01..06] --profile-mix "3x7g,1x20g" --dry-run
# bump warm pool
fleetctl warmpool scale --region=us-west2 --increment=20% --duration=3h
```

chris: +1 to the plan. suggest running rebalance dry-run then pick 2 hosts as canary before fleet-wide. watch for pci-e stall regressions. :eyes:

mike: also add a probe to check vGPU placement w.r.t root complexes. we had a case where carveouts still hit same complex due to rack cabling. small script suggestion: `lspci -tv` across candidate nodes and verify unique root paths.

taylor: I'll own the canary. timeline: start dry-run tonight at 23:00 UTC, canary rebalance + carveout tomorrow 02:00 UTC, monitor for 6h, then decide rollback or scale. who wants pager if things regress?

anya: I'll take pager for the first 3h of monitoring. chris on-call backup. notify #incidents if p50 > baseline + 30%.

sre-bot: Scheduled change created: CHANGE-7001 by taylor — dry-run at 2026-03-24T23:00:00Z. Runbook: https://wiki.redwood.internal/runbooks/mig-carveout-playbook. :white_check_mark:

chris: fine plan. also capture cost tag on carveouts so finance can track the temp bump.

taylor: noted. I'll add cost tags and update this thread with results. :thumbsup:
